Box Labels

LogicGame Strategy
Game: three boxes hold two white, two black, and one of each — but every label is wrong. Fix the labels after peeking at one ball.
How to play: click a box to see one ball. Click a label chip, then a box to place it. When all three are placed, press Verify.
Look for the math

Every label is wrong, so the assignment of labels to boxes is a derangement of the true contents. With three boxes there are only two derangements — both 3-cycles — and the applet picks one of them at random after shuffling the contents.

Open the mixed label

The box labelled white-and-black cannot really be mixed (that label would be right). So it holds two balls of one colour. The ball you see tells you which colour, and that box gets the matching same-colour label. The logic test checks that this always works for every deal the applet can make.

The rest follows

Of the two boxes left, one still wears the other same-colour label — which must also be wrong — so that box is the mixed one. The last label goes on the last box. One peek is enough; opening a same-colour box first may leave you unsure, just as the page says.

More boxes

With four boxes labelled WWW, WWB, WBB and BBB there are nine derangements, and two peeks never suffice. Three peeks can work with luck; four always can. That growth is why the three-box puzzle is the sweet spot.

Always open the box labelled WB first — then place the three labels without guessing.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
